moves.name: Posing the Core Question
moves.signature: A foundational assertion or question is established, defining the scope of the inquiry.
moves.anchor: Erdős conjectured

moves.name: Reframing the Central Problem
moves.signature: The initial problem is translated into an equivalent but more conceptually accessible form.
moves.anchor: no sign sequence has bounded discrepancy

moves.name: Reducing Infinite to Finite
moves.signature: An unbounded problem space is transformed into a bounded one, making it logically tractable.
moves.anchor: reduced this to a finite verification problem

moves.name: Establishing a Contingency
moves.signature: The solution to the primary problem is made dependent on the resolution of a separate, existing problem.
moves.anchor: via the Elliott conjecture

moves.name: Resolving a Key Dependency
moves.signature: A previously established conditional requirement is satisfied, unlocking the next stage of the main problem.
moves.anchor: proved the Elliott conjecture

moves.name: Adapting a Proven Method
moves.signature: A technique successful in a different context is modified and applied to the current problem.
moves.anchor: analogue of the entropy decrement argument

moves.name: Synthesizing Diverse Components
moves.signature: Several independent lines of reasoning or technical components are integrated into a single, coherent argument.
moves.anchor: combined three components

moves.name: Revealing Latent Structure
moves.signature: A formal statement is proven that describes the underlying organization or pattern of a central object of study.
moves.anchor: ergodic-theoretic structure theorem

moves.name: Bridging Formalisms
moves.signature: A dedicated argument is constructed to connect two different conceptual or technical frameworks.
moves.anchor: tying the structure theorem to discrepancy

moves.name: Amplifying a Weak Signal
moves.signature: A subtle or small effect is methodically strengthened until it becomes decisive for the argument.
moves.anchor: careful amplification of the entropy decrement

moves.name: Unifying Disparate Regimes
moves.signature: Results from fundamentally different domains, such as discrete and continuous, are reconciled and integrated.
moves.anchor: gluing the discrete and continuous estimates

moves.name: Leverage An Existing Result
moves.signature: Import a proven theorem from a simpler or more regular domain as a foundational component for the main argument.
moves.anchor: Szemerédi's theorem (arithmetic progressions in dense subsets of integers)

moves.name: Generalize The Target Domain
moves.signature: Extend a known principle from a specific, well-behaved context to a more abstract and broadly applicable class of structures.
moves.anchor: extended to subsets of a 'pseudorandom' set

moves.name: Define The Abstract Property
moves.signature: Establish a precise, operational definition for the abstract quality that enables the extended principle to function.
moves.anchor: define pseudorandomness via correlation conditions

moves.name: Execute A Transference Strategy
moves.signature: Prove a property for a complex object by showing it is a dense part of a simpler structure where the property is already known to hold.
moves.anchor: combinatorial transference

moves.name: Construct An Idealized Envelope
moves.signature: Embed the object of study within a larger, more well-behaved structure that possesses the desired analytical properties.
moves.anchor: sit inside a pseudorandom envelope

moves.name: Model Density Behavior
moves.signature: Create an auxiliary function that approximates the statistical or distributional properties of the primary object of study.
moves.anchor: construct a majorant function that captures prime density behavior

moves.name: Use A Weighted Proxy
moves.signature: Replace a simple indicator function with a weighted version that better captures the underlying structure and simplifies analysis.
moves.anchor: von Mangoldt λ-function

moves.name: Isolate The Core Difficulty
moves.signature: Pre-process the problem to remove known sources of irregularity, allowing the main argument to focus on the essential challenge.
moves.anchor: remove the small primes by sifting before applying transference

moves.name: Shift Burden To Estimation
moves.signature: Rely on establishing precise quantitative bounds rather than inventing new conceptual objects to carry the argument.
moves.anchor: Most of the argument's load is borne by combinatorial estimates

moves.name: Establish Alternate Pathway
moves.signature: Develop a new method to reach a known conclusion, bypassing the undesirable properties of an existing method.
moves.anchor: Their proof used ergodic theory and was long.

moves.name: Open Collaborative Search
moves.signature: Distribute the problem-solving process across a large, open community to explore many avenues in parallel.
moves.anchor: Polymath1 (organized by Gowers, 2009)

moves.name: Curate Collective Progress
moves.signature: Appoint a central agent to synthesize, organize, and steer contributions from a distributed group.
moves.anchor: with Gowers as moderator

moves.name: Adapt Proven Template
moves.signature: Modify a successful strategy from a different but related context to fit the current problem's requirements.
moves.anchor: in the spirit of Szemerédi's regularity lemma

moves.name: Monotonic Progress Iteration
moves.signature: Design a procedure that is applied repeatedly, with each application guaranteed to improve a specific, bounded metric.
moves.anchor: energy-increment iteration

moves.name: Isolate Invariant Property
moves.signature: Identify and formalize a key property that must be preserved through each step of a complex transformation.
moves.anchor: definition of 'partition regularity' for the increment step

moves.name: Reduce to Ideal Case
moves.signature: Prove the result for a simplified, more structured version of the problem, then show the general case follows from it.
moves.anchor: reduction to the case of a dense subset of an IP-rich set

moves.name: Synthesize from Components
moves.signature: Build a complete solution by developing a method for systematically combining smaller, more manageable pieces.
moves.anchor: finite combinatorial gluing

moves.name: Chain Bounding Arguments
moves.signature: Construct the final proof not from a single conceptual leap, but from a sequence of detailed, quantitative estimations.
moves.anchor: a sequence of specific combinatorial estimates

moves.name: Decompose into Uniformity
moves.signature: Partition a complex system into a collection of simpler, more uniform subsystems.
moves.anchor: every dense graph admits a partition of its vertices into ... regular pair

moves.name: Refine Through Iteration
moves.signature: Repeatedly apply a transformation to a state to progressively improve its quality according to some metric.
moves.anchor: proceeded by iterative refinement

moves.name: Guide with Potential
moves.signature: Define a scalar quantity that monotonically changes with each step of a process, ensuring progress and termination.
moves.anchor: using mean-square energy as a potential function

moves.name: Start with Triviality
moves.signature: Initiate a process from the simplest possible configuration of the system.
moves.anchor: starting with the trivial partition

moves.name: Bound the Process
moves.signature: Establish an upper limit on the resources or steps required to reach a solution, even if the limit is extremely large.
moves.anchor: bound the iteration by a tower-of-twos

moves.name: Leverage the Structure
moves.signature: Use the properties of a structured decomposition to derive a conclusion about the original system.
moves.anchor: The triangle removal lemma followed from regularity

moves.name: Aggregate Across Components
moves.signature: Infer a global property by counting or summing interactions between the constituent parts of a partitioned system.
moves.anchor: counting edges between regular pairs containing triangles

moves.name: Link Local to Global
moves.signature: Establish a quantitative relationship between a local structural property and a global modification.
moves.anchor: if a graph has o(n^3) triangles then they can be made triangle-free by removing o(n^2) edges

moves.name: Generalize the Apparatus
moves.signature: Apply a proven method or result to solve problems in different, seemingly unrelated domains.
moves.anchor: Applied to Roth's theorem, Behrend constructions, Ramsey theory, additive combinatorics

moves.name: Prioritize Quantitative Bounds
moves.signature: Achieve a result by establishing quantitative estimates and relationships rather than by constructing new entities.
moves.anchor: The proofs were combinatorial estimates, not new objects
